newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may announce big privatisations next week.
newsitem.headline: Russia may announce big privatisations next week.

text.p: Russia may announce details next Tuesday of its plans to auction a 25 percent plus one share stake in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said on Thursday.
Kokh also told the the State Duma lower house of parliament that planned auctions of stakes in a series of oil companies could start next week.
"Details of the Svyazinvest auction will be announced in the near future, on Tuesday, I think," Kokh said. "The sale of the oil companies, I think, will start next week."
The government is launching a round of major sell-offs as it seeks to boost the role of privatisation revenues in funding the budget deficit.

Kokh said the State Property Committee, Russia's privatisation ministry, now intended to raise 11.4 trillion roubles from privatisation this year, instead of the 6.4 trillion stipulated in the 1997 budget.

The bulk of this money will come from the sale of Svyazinvest and of a series of oil companies the state does not consider strategic enterprises -- Vostsibneftegaz, Vostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Eastern Oil), Sibirsko-Uralskaya Neftegazokhimicheskaya Kompaniya (Sibur), Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya, KomiTEK and Norsi-Oil.
Kokh said the oil company auctions would be conducted in a new way, with bids accepted over several months and the results announced in the autumn.
The government said last month the stake in OAO Svyazinvest would have a starting price of $1.18 billion. Kokh has previously estimated proceeds from it at $1.5-2.0 billion.
Duma deputies have often said the Svyazinvest stake should be sold only to Russian investors, but it is on offer to both Russian and foreign portfolio investors.
It will be sold to a single bidder. The government is selling a further 24 percent of Svyazinvest at an investment tender open only to Russian investors.
"I have never thought that we had to be completely of one mind with the Duma on this question," Kokh said.
The government is transferring its controlling stake in long-distance operator Rostelekom to Svyazinvest, as well as stakes in three other companies, in time for the sale.
This will result in a capital increase of Svyazinvest, with 49 percent of the enlarged capital planned to be sold off.
